title: StakeholderAnalysisOutput
description: Structured stakeholder analysis output: stakeholder profiles, power-interest mapping, coalition dynamics, risks, engagement plans, and next actions — all grounded in transcript evidence.

executive_summary.description: 2-4 sentence overview of the stakeholder landscape: who matters most, key alignments and tensions, and the single biggest engagement risk.

decision_surface.description: The core decision or initiative that the stakeholder analysis is oriented around, inferred from the transcript or provided via focal_decision.

stakeholders.description: Profiled stakeholders identified from the transcript and/or stakeholder_directory. Each includes stance, influence, evidence, and engagement-relevant attributes.

power_interest_map.description: Power-interest grid mapping for each stakeholder. Determines engagement strategy quadrant.

coalition_dynamics.description: Analysis of likely alliances, blockers, swing stakeholders, and relationship risks across the stakeholder group.

risks.description: Stakeholder-related risks that could derail the decision or initiative. Each includes severity, likelihood, early signals, and mitigation.

engagement_plan.description: Tailored engagement actions for key stakeholders. Each specifies messaging, channel, timing, and success criteria.

next_7_day_actions.description: Concrete actions for the next 7 days to advance stakeholder alignment. Each has an owner, due date, and proof artifact.

open_questions.description: Unresolved questions about stakeholder positions, motivations, or dynamics that require further investigation.

citations.description: Verbatim quotes from the transcript that ground the analysis. Referenced by stakeholder profiles, risks, and engagement plans.

metadata.description: Analysis metadata: which input mode was used and when the output was generated.

recommended_path.description: Optional best-path recommendation. Populated with the 'actionable' variant when the analysis has high confidence (3+ evidence-backed stakeholders and 2+ risks with early signals). Uses the 'insufficient_information' variant when evidence gaps prevent a clear recommendation, explaining what additional context is needed.

name.description: Stakeholder's name as identified in the transcript.

role.description: Job title or organizational role inferred from the transcript or stakeholder_directory.

influence_level.description: Assessed organizational influence over the decision. 'critical' = can unilaterally block or approve.

stance.description: Stakeholder's apparent position on the focal decision based on transcript evidence.

evidence.description: Verbatim quotes or near-verbatim evidence from the transcript supporting the stance and influence assessment.

goals.description: What this stakeholder is trying to achieve, inferred from their statements and behavior in the transcript.

concerns.description: Explicit or implicit worries, objections, or reservations expressed by this stakeholder.

hidden_incentives_or_constraints.description: Inferred motivations, political pressures, or constraints not explicitly stated but suggested by context or behavior.

alignment_score.description: 0-100 score reflecting how aligned this stakeholder is with the focal decision. 0 = fully opposed, 100 = fully supportive.

change_readiness.description: How ready this stakeholder is to accept and act on the proposed change. Considers both willingness and capacity.

name.description: Stakeholder name, matching a name in the stakeholders array.

power.description: Organizational power to influence or block the decision. 1 = minimal, 5 = decisive authority.

interest.description: Level of active interest in the decision outcome. 1 = indifferent, 5 = deeply invested.

quadrant.description: Engagement quadrant derived from power and interest. manage_closely = high power + high interest. keep_satisfied = high power + low interest. keep_informed = low power + high interest. monitor = low power + low interest.

likely_allies.description: Stakeholders likely to support and champion the decision.

likely_blockers.description: Stakeholders likely to resist or actively block the decision.

swing_stakeholders.description: Stakeholders whose position is uncertain and could tip either way. High-value engagement targets.

relationship_risks.description: Interpersonal or inter-team dynamics that pose risk to alignment or execution.

id.description: Unique identifier for this risk. Format: SR-001, SR-002, etc.

title.description: Concise, specific risk title tied to concrete stakeholder dynamics.

severity.description: Impact magnitude if this risk materializes. 1 = minor friction, 5 = project failure or political crisis.

likelihood.description: Probability of occurrence given current stakeholder dynamics. 1 = very unlikely, 5 = near certain.

owner_recommendation.description: Who should own mitigation of this risk.

early_signals.description: Observable signals that this risk is materializing. Specific enough to monitor week-over-week.

mitigation.description: Concrete, actionable step to reduce severity or likelihood. Not a restatement of the risk.

stakeholder.description: Name of the stakeholder this engagement targets.

objective.description: What you want to achieve in this engagement. Example: 'Secure budget approval', 'Surface hidden concerns'.

message_frame.description: How to frame the message for this stakeholder given their stance, goals, and concerns.

ask.description: The specific request or call-to-action for this stakeholder.

channel.description: Recommended communication channel for this engagement.

timing.description: When this engagement should happen. Example: 'Before Thursday's steering committee', 'Within 48 hours'.

owner.description: Who is responsible for executing this engagement step.

success_signal.description: Observable indicator that the engagement achieved its objective.

action.description: Specific action to take within the next 7 days.

owner.description: Person responsible for completing this action.

due.description: Due date or time window. Example: 'Monday EOD', '2026-03-15', 'Before steering committee'.

proof_artifact.description: Tangible output proving this action was completed. Example: 'Shared doc link in #channel', 'Email confirmation from VP'.

approximate_location.description: Where in the transcript this appears. Examples: 'opening remarks', 'during budget discussion', 'closing action items'.

mode_used.description: Which input mode was detected. transcript_only if no optional context fields were provided; transcript_plus_context otherwise.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this analysis was generated.

status.description: Indicates the analysis has sufficient confidence to recommend a concrete path forward.

overall_recommendation.description: 1-3 sentence synthesis of the best path forward: who to engage first, what to prioritize, and the key unlock.

leverage.description: Stakeholders to lean on and amplify. These are allies or sponsors whose support accelerates the decision.

improve_relations.description: Stakeholders where investing relationship capital will yield the highest return. Typically skeptics or swing voters with legitimate concerns.

watch_list.description: Stakeholders to monitor for early warning signals. Not necessarily adversaries — may be allies at risk of disengagement.

status.description: Indicates the analysis lacks sufficient confidence to recommend a clear path forward.

overall_recommendation.description: Explains why a clear path cannot be recommended and what the primary evidence gaps are.

information_gaps.description: Specific pieces of missing information or context that prevent a confident recommendation.

suggested_next_steps.description: Actions the user should take to close the information gaps and enable a confident recommendation on re-run.

stakeholder.description: Name of the stakeholder to leverage.

why.description: Why this stakeholder is a leverage point — their power, access, or credibility.

how.description: Specific action to activate this stakeholder's support.

stakeholder.description: Name of the stakeholder to invest in.

why.description: Why this relationship needs investment — unaddressed concerns, trust deficit, or strategic importance.

how.description: Specific action to improve the relationship — what to do, say, or deliver.

stakeholder.description: Name of the stakeholder to monitor.

signal.description: Observable behavior or event that indicates a risk is materializing with this stakeholder.

contingency.description: What to do if the signal fires.
